title: MLabs - Cardano Game Engine Wallet - Godot Integration

ms.promise:
・Research write-up on Godot 4’s extension systems, explaining cons and pros for the current project. It should explain why developing a full SDK compared to just a wallet is feasible or not.
・Proof-of-concept integration of either CTL / Lucid (if developing a SDK is feasible) or CSL (if only developing a light wallet is feasible). The POC should consist of a demo that shows: GDScript code calling into the integrated codebase and performing one of its intended functions. The POC may showcase trivial and incomplete functionality, it is only intended to demonstrate that calling into the chosen library and obtaining results is possible. The POC may run only in the Godot editor (and not in exported games) and in a single operating system (as opposed to all supported OS). Portability is a later goal and the POC should not be judged based on this.
・Paima integration design based on conversations with dcSpark.

As previously communicated in a Change Request form with the Catalyst team, this project will have a delayed start of 1 month, otherwise, starting in November. This only affects the project timeline moderately, and does not affect the budget or scope of our deliverables.

ms.report:
Milestone 3 Proof of Achievement
Milestone outputs
The following features have been implemented in Rust and are accessible within the Godot engine:
・Generating and importing single-address wallets
・Encrypting and storing generated wallets to the user data directory
・Balancing, signing, and submitting transactions

In addition, based on the conclusion in Milestone 1 that an SDK was viable, we have provided the following features:
・UTxO querying for wallet and script addresses via Blockfrost
・Including Plutus scripts and evaluating the transaction for validity and fee calculation
・Producing and consuming Plutus script inputs
・Minting Cardano native tokens from Plutus scripts

The above features can be tested manually via the demo app provided, while more thorough testing is available by running the integration tests as described in the README document (https://github.com/mlabs-haskell/godot-cardano?tab=readme-ov-file#run-integration-test). 

Test results
The test suite should complete after 3-5 minutes and success should be indicated in the console output. The transactions can be viewed in a Preview blockchain explorer. For example:
Funding transaction (https://preview.cexplorer.io/tx/8b93edbe57a8c9ec50ef8c523432e977767b52db8e616ecfec6ef07825293b20)
Return transaction (https://preview.cexplorer.io/tx/67b01c1cdab4a803e799681f79baf26760ab52cfe8703a4ccf2565503bf1a19c)

In the above transactions, funds are sent to multiple temporary addresses to run SDK feature tests in parallel, after which they are collected and returned to the primary address. Corresponding transactions should be visible for your own wallet after having run the test suite successfully.

Example feature testing transactions:
Plutus script input spending (https://preview.cexplorer.io/tx/255a8952ca76c3fafc30a974f7054499bd4aa74e08aa230cb03ee880b6dad10e)
Plutus token minting(https://preview.cexplorer.io/tx/7b1643785c18063b5f327db2b38bf4c9399b4154521a6c2b3038e1c77357723c)

ms.promise: A modified Paima engine that allows developers to create systems for players to sign and submit transactions.
ms.criteria:
・All of the functionality should be accessible from the API.
・Each implemented function should be documented with its purpose and examples of use.
・A test suite should cover all of the use cases.
ms.report:
The output for this milestone is a modified Paima engine that allows developers to create systems for players to sign and submit transactions. As per the acceptance criteria, all the functionality is accessible from the API, functions are properly documented and the use cases have been appropriately tested.
EVIDENCE OF MILESTONE COMPLETION
Outputs:
* Newly committed code modules for the developed API.
Available as new add'ons "cip-30-callbacks" and "paima-middleware" under the addon/@mlabs-haskell folder.
All functionality is provided by these two addons:
 1. "cip-30-callbacks" is used to register godot-cardano as a CIP-30 compatible wallet in the browser window.
 2. "paima-middleware" provides functions for logging into Paima and querying the round executor component of the Paima framework

# Note on documentation:
Detailed documentation on each class and method is provided as inline comments in the relevant files. Documentation is provided as GDScript doc comments so all public classes intended to be used by the final user can be queried inside the engine. Specifically, for the files inside the folders "cip-30-callbacks" and "paima-middleware", a description of the class is provided at the top level of the file, along with descriptions throughout the files for each of the functions intended to be used by the user.
 
* Test results showcasing successful execution of all features.
A Godot project based on Paima's open world template was created, showcasing the use of the entirety of the API. A demonstration
of it is made in the close-out video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YuFD4gi2Qnc.
A README file is provided under paima-demo with instruction to set up all the different Paima components needed and the setup for exporting the demo to the web.
